content:
Apple has raised prices on most of its products in recent months, but iPhone and other products are expected to see further price hikes next month.

iPhone 18 series is expected to go up in price, with Apple Watch and AirPods also potentially affected

Earlier this summer, Apple had already raised prices on some of its product lines.

Mac, iPad, Apple TV, HomePod and Vision Pro all saw price increases at the same time.

CEO Tim Cook had warned in advance about price hikes, but the sheer breadth of products hit in one go still came as a shock.

The flagship products that escaped unscathed in that round of price increases included:

  • iPhone
  • Apple Watch
  • AirPods

At the time, Apple hinted that more price hikes were on the way, and analysts believed those that had temporarily dodged the bullet would soon face increases too.

Fast forward to the September iPhone 18 launch event, and a price hike for iPhone is pretty much a given.

Rumour has it that the starting price of the iPhone 18 Pro will be between US$1,299 and US$1,399, compared with US$1,099 for the iPhone 17 Pro.

Apple has typically lowered the prices of older models when launching new ones. However, this year the older models are expected to hold their prices steady — or even edge up slightly.

Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 could both see price increases, as the AI-driven memory crunch is also affecting component costs for Apple Watch.

Finally, AirPods may also see a price hike — though the chances are slimmer compared with iPhone and Apple Watch, since rising memory and storage chip costs should have less impact on AirPods.

But if Apple is really planning to raise prices across the entire lineup, and that includes AirPods, we'll most likely find out at the September event.

What pricing moves do you expect from Apple? Let us know in the comments.
